description.text: AI-written synthesis of the cited official pages, prepared by the collecting assistant: MassChallenge operates several accelerators rather than one uniform cohort. Its Traction programs support early commercialization, while Challenge programs connect startups with corporate partners for design partnerships, pilots, proofs of concept, and commercial adoption. Its stated focus areas include Healthcare & Life Sciences, Security & Resiliency, Sustainable Food Systems, Climate, and Global Financial Systems. MassChallenge does not take equity; its 2026 Security & Resiliency Traction FAQ also explicitly says that program has no participation fee. The 2026–2027 Challenge Cycle publishes a November 9, 2026 application deadline and February–June 2027 programming with required Boston events. Separately, the 16-week hybrid SMU Cox FinTech Accelerator publishes a November 19, 2026 deadline and three required Dallas immersions. These are program-specific opportunities, not one organization-wide schedule or guaranteed investment offer.

targetApplicants.text: AI-written synthesis of the cited official pages, prepared by the collecting assistant: MassChallenge's Traction offering addresses pre-seed through Series A startups. For the 2026–2027 Challenge Cycle, startups must address at least one published partner challenge; partners work in FinTech, Insurance, and Healthcare & Life Sciences, but relevant solutions can come from other fields. That cycle accepts startups from around the world and requires at least one founder or C-suite representative at specified Boston events. The SMU Cox accelerator separately welcomes founders across financial innovation, including capital markets, financial-services AI, blockchain, cybersecurity, and an open-topic track. Applicants should choose the individual program before treating its stage, travel requirements, timing, or economics as applicable to them.

sources.title: MassChallenge — accelerator families and Traction stages
sources.quote:
Our programs deliver the next generation of founder support, combining deep sector expertise with the networks and pathways required to reach real customers and adoption. We prioritize commercialization—not valuation—so the world’s most ambitious founders can move from idea to impact faster.

TRACTION PROGRAMS

For pre-seed to Series A startups.

Our Traction Program focuses on go-to-market, strategic exposure, and the early commercialization that opens doors to customers and investors.

CHALLENGE PROGRAMS

Where industry priorities become pipelines.

Our Challenge Program is a partner driven accelerator that opens the door to work with powerhouse corporate partners, co-create solutions, and scale what matters most.

sources.title: MassChallenge Challenge programs — commercial collaboration model
sources.quote:
DESIGN PARTNERSHIP

Where solutions take shape. Founders work directly with industry experts to refine their technology through feedback and real-world insight.

PILOTS

Where ideas meet real conditions. Founders test solutions alongside industry leaders to prove feasibility and fit.

PROOFS OF CONCEPT

Early validation that turns potential into proof. Together, founders and partners test what works and why it matters.

COMMERCIALIZATION

When collaboration becomes traction, breakthroughs move from pilot to market with partners ready to scale.

sources.title: MassChallenge — published zero-equity policy
sources.quote: MassChallenge assists startups with growth, connection to resources, and access to industry-leading mentors—but does not take equity.

sources.title: 2026 Security & Resiliency Traction — no fee, no equity, self-funded travel
sources.quote:
Is there a cost to participate?

No. this is a no-cost, non-dilutive accelerator program, meaning there is no program fee and we don’t take equity.

[…]

Do you provide travel reimbursement or stipends?

No, at this time, we do not provide travel reimbursement or stipends. All travel-related costs are self-funded.

sources.title: 2026–2027 Challenge Cycle — deadline, eligibility, participation, and program contact
sources.quote:
APPLY BY NOVEMBER 9, 2026

[…]

We’re looking for pre-seed to Series A startups whose solutions address one or more of our partners’ published challenge statements. Our partners are leaders in FinTech, Insurance and Healthcare & Life Sciences, but their challenges often go beyond those industries, so read through the challenge statements even if your startup works in another field. At least one founder or C-suite team member must attend the required in-person events in Boston: Matchmaking (January 6 to 8, 2027, for finalists only), Kickoff & Orientation (February 9 to 10, 2027) and the program close-out event in mid-June 2027.

[…]

No, we accept applications from startups from around the world.

[…]

The program runs from February to June 2027. Plan on spending 3 to 5 hours a week working with your partner, including meetings with them about twice a month, depending on their schedule.

[…]

There’s also a virtual mid-program day in April.

[…]

Send an email to programs@masschallenge.org.

sources.title: SMU Cox FinTech Accelerator — separate deadline, format, and focus areas
sources.quote:
